Ajanta Cave 10, a Satavahana-era chaitya, carries the painting of the Shwetagaja (Chhadanta) Jataka (G2 2012). The notes do not link the Vessantara, Mahajanaka or Sibi Jatakas to this cave.

Haravilasam is the Reddi-period text on sea trade (G2 2019 key). Kashikhandam is the trap: the G2 2011 key gave it, but follow the later key. Kalachakra and the Amaravati Mahachaitya have nothing to do with Reddi sea trade.

Nagarjuna's Suhrullekha ('friendly letter') was addressed to his patron and close friend Yajna Sri Satakarni. Hala and Kuntala Satakarni were other Satavahana kings, and Gunadhya was the author of the Brihatkatha.

All four are correct. Madhava Varma II pushed the Vakatakas back to the Godavari coast and took Karma-rashtra up to the Gundlakamma from the Pallavas. He also took Vengi from the Salankayanas and reached north Andhra in his 37th year. So D.

The order is A, B, C, D (option B). Indrabhattaraka (525-555) was killed in the Kalinga war first. Prithvi Maharaja broke away at Pishtapuram under his successor Vikramendra Varma II (555-569). Pulakeshin II defeated Manchana Bhattaraka at Kunala in 624 CE, and his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana then founded the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi. Option A puts the breakaway before Indrabhattaraka's death. Options C and D put the 624 CE defeat before the breakaway.

The wrong pair is C. The Khanapur plates come from Satara district in Maharashtra, and Ramatirtham is Indravarma's record, so neither belongs to the Guntur region. The other pairs follow the notes: Ipur and Velpuru are in Guntur, Chikkulla and Polamuru in the Godavari region, and Tummalagudem in Telangana.
